title: Repair a relative dangling link
goal: Resolve a relative link from its containing directory and repair only the link.
challenge: Repair a dangling link in a nested directory while preserving the original bytes and metadata. Verify access from two different current directories and retain the relative target string.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/local-symlinks.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/local-symlinks.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here
steps.explanation: Create a unique learner-owned guest workspace; stop on error and record its absolute path. Reopening boots the disk, not these shell variables. Never use the host terminal.
steps.expected: A new private directory; no pre-existing files are changed.

steps.command: here && fresh docs links before.sha256 before.meta && { mkdir docs links; printf 'handover\n' > docs/note.txt; chmod 0640 docs/note.txt; sha256sum docs/note.txt > before.sha256; stat -c '%a %h' docs/note.txt > before.meta; ln -s ../missing/note.txt links/current; }
steps.explanation: The fault is a wrong relative target. A dangling link exists even when test -e is false.

steps.command: here && { readlink links/current; test -L links/current && test ! -e links/current; cat links/current; printf "read status=%s\n" "$?"; }
steps.explanation: Relative targets resolve from links/, not the current shell directory. Capture the failed read without claiming the original is missing.
steps.expected: Known wrong target and a failed read.

steps.command: here && { test -L links/current && rm -- links/current && ln -s ../docs/note.txt links/current; }
steps.explanation: Replace only the verified link. Do not overwrite docs/note.txt or use ln -sf on an ambiguous path.

steps.command: here && { readlink links/current; cat links/current; (cd links && cat current); sha256sum -c before.sha256; test "$(stat -c '%a %h' docs/note.txt)" = "$(cat before.meta)"; }
steps.explanation: Verify resolution from both directories, independent bytes and metadata.
steps.expected: Both reads handover; unchanged original bytes/mode/link count.

hints: Read the link before changing it.
Change the link, then verify the original independently.
review: I retained actual output and checked the required contents, metadata or identity, not just command success.
I can explain the stated limitations, demonstrate the incorrect case, preserve originals and clean up only my recorded workspace.
